Bishops of Geneva: Cariatto, 582; Rusticus, or Patricius, 604 n.; Domitianus, 1318 n. Genialis, duke of the Vascones, 604. Genitor, citizen, 1107. Gennensis, a village, 1124 n. Genobaud, or Genobald, duke of the Franks, 57. Was he a king? 60 n. Genoliacum monastery, 980 n. Genovefa, most blessed, 141. Famous for miracles, 97 n. Her basilica, 125 n., 141, 142 n. The Parisian virgin, 973. Her monastery, ibid., n.

Genseric, king of the Vandals, 44 n., 45 n. Genuliacum, 1311. Geometry deals with measurements, 538. Georgia, consecrated virgin, 921. Her tomb, etc., 922. Epitaph and relics, 1401. Relics of the martyr George, 833. George, count of Auvergne, 922. George, father of Saint Gall, 1169. Gregory’s grandfather, 1222. Cunimund, king of the Gepids, 182 n.

Gereon and the other Theban martyrs, 793 n. Gerinus, brother of Saint Leodegarius, is killed, 666. Martyr, 1397.

Germany: the Franks invade it, 57, 59. They are driven out from there, 549. Chrocus devastates it, 711. Attila spares its cities, 708. The people of Germany, 1140. Its nations, 61. Its peoples fight with Pompey, 706. Saint Columbanus shines there, 611. Two Germanies in Gaul, 77 and n., 1391. First Germany, 960.

Germanus, bishop of Auxerre, [Col. 1239] 871, 955 n. His basilica and monastery, 219, 928 n. Miracles, 339, 928. Germanus, bishop of Paris, 161 n., 214, 284, 464, 1281, 1341. He excommunicates Charibert for incest, 166. His prophecy concerning Sigibert, 194, 575. Letter to Brunichild, 192 n., 1343. He attends the feast of Saint Martin, 1045. He attends the translation of Saint Ursinus, 963. He blesses the abbess Agnes, 473. He completes the cursus during journeys, 424 n. He spends the night in prayer, 974. He dies, 211, 577. Translation, 1370. Famous for miracles, 211, 972. His deeds, 973. Book of his life, 211. Psalter, 1381. Buried in the basilica of Saint Vincent, 406. It was thereafter called the basilica of Saint Germanus of the Meadows, 211, 326 n., 382 n. Childebert, kings, queens, princes, etc., were buried in it, 1378, 1379. Statues of the ancient kings, 1371. Monastery, 131 n., 626 n. It is called a distinguished place, 410 n. Its history, 1369. See Saint Vincent.

—Church of Saint Germanus at Tours, 534. Church of Licaniacum, 71. —Germanus, prefect of Rome, 481. —The Germans wore torques, 128 n. They come to Ravenna, 707. They seize Spain and invade Syria, 707. They were praetorian soldiers, 770 n. Custom concerning wives’ dowries, 294 n. Thus the Franks are called, 548 n. Head of the Germanic peoples: Rheims, 163 n.

Gerontius creates a tyrant, 61. Gerunda, a city, 824. The body of Gervasius at Milan, 775. Basilica and relics in Gaul; history of the Passion, 776. Church at Rome, 482. At Tours, 1396. Where the relics are, 529, 534. Deeds of the Franks, a book attributed to Gregory, 83 n.

Gezalicus, king of the Goths, 94 n. Ghiselarius, count of Bourges, 701. Gehazi’s leprosy, 790. Gildardus, bishop: Gregory’s antiphon concerning him, 1283. Giscladus, son of Saint Sigismund, 110 n. Gislemar, having displaced his father, becomes mayor of the palace and dies, 669. Giso, citizen of Saintonge, 1106. Gisoulfus submits to the emperor, 1348.

Givald, son of Sigivald, 127. He escapes death, 128. He returns to Theudebert, 129. The disaster at Glandolaria, 602. Glicerius, bishop of Couserans, 440 n. When dormice were first seen at Paris, 407. Father of Glodesindis, 601 n. Her parents, monastery, etc., 390 n.

“Glory in the highest,” etc., 794, 1055. “Glory be to the Father,” etc.: how it is to be said, 316, 317. “Glory to the Trinity” concludes the singing, 760. The glorification of the Son by the Father, 318. Goaesinda, wife of Leuvigild, 580. Goar, 61.

Godegisel, king of the Burgundians, 80, 557. Betrayer of his brother, 85, 561. He triumphs at Vienne, 86, 561. There he is besieged, 87. He is killed, 88, 562. Unfortunate on account of heresy, 104.

Godegisil, king of the Vandals, 61. Godegisel, duke of Sigibert, 193. Godegisil, son-in-law of Duke Lupus, acting as duke, 431, 432. Whether he was another person from the duke, 432 n.

Godemar, king of the Burgundians, 557, 564. Driven out by Chlodomer, he regains strength, 109. Defeated again and restored, 110. Driven out, 114. Unfortunate on account of heresy, 104. Godfrid, duke, 684. Godinus, 202. He dies, 203. Godinus, son of Warnacharius, 631. He is killed, 632.

[Col. 1259]

Gogo, royal tutor, 259; he dies, 271. Gogo, ambassador of Sigibert to Spain, 570. He becomes mayor of the palace, 571. He is killed, 571. Goisvintha, queen, 247. Wife of Leuvigild and mother of Brunichild; she makes a treaty with Reccared, 419. Then she plots against him, 419 n., 436. Her cruelty toward Ingund, 248.

Goliath overthrown, 1208. A foreigner, 39. Killed by David, 275. Gomacharius, count of Agde, 810. He dies, 811. Gomatrudis marries Dagobert, 630. She is dismissed, 635. Gordinis, a fortress, 700. Gosvinta’s plot against Reccared, 436 n.

Gotefrid, duke of the Alamanni, 1353. Gothesil. See Godegisel. Gothia, 195. Gothic region, 679.

—Goths, 337, 454. Their kingdom, 272. Their boundaries, 679. They crush the Romans, 29. They capture Rome, 60. Their settlements in Gaul, 63. Where they rule, 399. In Spain, 903. They held Tours, 1242. They fight against Attila, 708, 709. They drive out the Britons, 70. And slaughter them, 555. They regard Catholic bishops with suspicion, 532. Saint Quintianus, 1160. The Gauls, because of the proximity of the Franks, 91. They lose many possessions, 95. Defeated by Chlodovech, 93, 533. After his death they invade what they had lost, 127. They capture Arles, 128. Driven out by Ecdicius, 77, or Aedicius, 555. Likewise by Desiderius, 416. They hold the bishopric of Arisitum, 207. They subjugate Galicia and the Suebi, 580. Defeated by the Franks, 562, 711. They crush the Franks, 455 n., 600. They subjugate Cantabria and several cities, 610. Incursion into Provence, 425. King Pippin seeks redress for the Goths killed by Waifarius, 693. Embassies, 321, etc.

—The Goths are Arians, 933. They become Catholics, 450, 598. Custom of killing kings, 131, 553, 653. It is suppressed, 654. In the councils, 131 n. Custom concerning wives’ dowries, 294 n. Liars, 709, 710. Accustomed to flight, 94. Custom of fear, 78, 556. End of their kingdom in Italy, 566. See Ostrogoths, Visigoths, 556.

Kings of the Goths: Athanaric, 51. Alaric the Great, 56, etc. Theodoric, 707, etc. Thorismund, or Thursemodus, 646, 708, etc. Euric, 71, etc. Called Evaric, 77, etc. Alaric, 556, etc. Amalaric, 94, etc. Gezalicus, 94 n. Reccared, 598, etc. See Spain.

Gracina, an island, 260 n. Epiphanius, bishop of Grado, 298 n. The Gradual in the Mass, 378 n. Psalms of the Steps, 1258. Chilperic adopts Greek letters, 258. Blessed Greece, which heard Paul, 1000. Its sages, 1140.

—The Greeks occupy Pannonia, 707. They recover part of Spain and are then defeated, 147 n. They deceive Hermenegild, 249. They detain his wife Ingund, 316, 320, 582. The first emperor of their race is Maurice, 303 n.

Grafio Ingobodus, 622. Grafiones, 647. Who they are, 622 n. Grammar teaches reading, 538.

Gradiswintha. See Gunthsuentha. Grasoulfus rebels against the emperor, 1248. Grata, martyr at Lyons, 779. Necessity of grace, 16, 992. Its effects, 465, 1393. Gratianopolis, a city, 186. Hesychius, bishop of Gratianopolis, 470. Gratian, emperor, 29. [Col. 1240] Gratian, bishop of Tours. See Gatianus. Gratian of Sinope, 1262. Gratus, consul, 23. —Age of Gratus, bishop of Augsburg, 1318 n.

Gredonense, a fortress, 26 and n. The age of Pope Gregory the Great, 538. He founds monasteries, ibid. Monastic life, 479 n. He confutes Eutychius, bishop of Constantinople, 497 n. He had lifted the son of the emperor Maurice from the baptismal font, 481. His virtues and election, 480. Address to the people, 481. He institutes processions, 482. Consecrated in the church of Saint Peter, 483. He gives relics to the deacon of Saint Gregory of Tours, 483. His stature is admired, Life, n. 42. He forbids Jews to be compelled to the faith, 213 n. He labors for the conversion of the Angles, 165 n. He wishes the Angles to be educated in the monasteries of Gaul, 214 n. Peter the deacon admirably defends his writings, 1403.

Embassy of Gregory III to Charles Martel, 680. Gregory, bishop of Antioch, 599, 600. Gregory, bishop of Langres, 122, 126, 155, 156 n., 208, 780. Previously count of Autun, 1178. He transfers the body of Saint Benignus, 781. He builds a church, 782. His Life, 1177. Translation, 1181.

Attalus, Gregory’s nephew, 119. Captive, 565.

Gregory of Tours, bishop, born on the feast of Saint Andrew, 1264. His age, etc., 538. A special disciple of Saint Julian, 850, 886. Taught by Saint Avitus the bishop, 1153. His brother Peter, 206, etc. Nicetius, bishop, his mother’s maternal uncle, 208. Likewise Gundulf, duke, 287. His uncle Gallus, bishop, 867. His niece Eusthenia, 1135. His sister’s husband Justinus, 1040. Almost all his kinsmen were bishops of Tours, 267. He vows that he will become a cleric, 1155. While still a deacon, his merit, 1031. He becomes bishop of Tours, 536. Time of his ordination, 1037. In his thirty-fourth year, he is consecrated at Rheims, 1087, 176 n. He visits Lyons and then Vienne, 850. Lyons, 944, 971. He arrives at Paris, 424. He stays at Châlons, 948. He visits his mother in Burgundy, 1032. Chalon-sur-Saône, 1111. He goes to Auvergne, 1111. Now bishop, he visits Auvergne and Brioude, 874. He visits the tomb of Saint Solemnis, 1400. Of Saint Hilary, 725. And venerates the cross in the monastery of Saint Radegund, 726, whose funeral he celebrates, 985.

The king entrusts him with the affair of Ingeltrudis, 458. He is sent to suppress disturbances in the monastery at Poitiers, 504. He visits Childebert’s court, 1129. He remains there, 1130. He passes through Rheims, 432. Childebert receives him at a feast, 385. He is with him at Orléans, 1135. He returns to Tours, 1136. At the court of Guntram, 376. Guntram visits and invites him to a feast, 378 ff. Ambassador to Childebert, 444, 445. To Guntram, 439. He visits Chilperic, 272, 274. He is accused before him, 260, 262. He clears himself at three altars, 265. He denies Leudast communion, 306. His dispute with Felix, bishop of Nantes, 206. Vision concerning Chilperic, etc., 217, 379. He exhorts the people of Tours to peace, 371.

—Gregory of Tours’s profession of faith, 6. Confession of the most holy Trinity, 104. He refutes the Arians, 253, 316. He proves the Resurrection against a presbyter, 497. He rebukes Chilperic for dogmatizing, 257. He disputes against the Jews, 275 ff. Observer of the canons, 291. Courage in defending Praetextatus, 223. Against the king, 224, 225. He rejects silver, 225. He defends the exemption of Tours from taxation, 453. He was the first of all to commend in writing the bodily Assumption of blessed Mary into heaven, 723 n. His care for monks, 1254. He visits Friardus, 1209. He offers drink to robbers, 1032. He completes the cursus in the church at midnight, 424. There he sings psalms, 347. His visions, ibid., 927.

He restores basilicas and builds a baptistery, 537. He rebuilds a church, etc. He visits the relics of the saints, 336, 1396. He establishes an oratory of the Holy Cross, 467 n. He solemnly dedicates his oratory, 909. He receives relics from Rome, 479, 483, 1189. He is healed by Saint Illidius, 1154, 1155. Likewise at the fountain of Saint Julian, 868. By the merits of Saint Martin, 1029. Even when close to death, 1038. Having drunk dust from Saint Martin’s tomb, 1039. Or by touching the veil, 1117. By touching the grille, ibid., 1076, 1082. As had his mother, 1087. He carried the relics of Saint Martin with him, 1091. Dust from the tomb, 1135. The cross containing the relics of the saints, 735. He possesses Saint Medard’s staff, 977. He is punished for vanity, 817. His relics, 1391. His life and eulogies precede his works.

—Commendation of the works of Gregory of Tours, preface, 4. He excuses his style, 1197. He confesses that he is uneducated, 5. Unlearned, 852. Rough in speech and inexperienced, 891. An ignorant and unpolished man, 995. The rusticity of his style in himself, 1153. His style, etc., preface, 62. Credulity, preface, 64. Sincerity, preface, 67. Simplicity, preface, 68. Caution, preface, 69. Whether he contradicts himself, preface, 101.

He wished to write only what happened after the deaths of the saints, 1143, and things otherwise unknown, preface, 71. He lists his works, 537, 893. He implores that they not be altered, 537. Gregory’s works are listed and discussed, preface, 72 ff. The order in which they were written, preface, 83. Their titles, preface, 85. Their integrity is defended against Cointius, preface, 86 ff. Need for a new edition, preface, 2. Its usefulness, preface, 5. Manuscripts and editions compared, preface, 122 ff. Why some are shorter in certain places, preface, 90.

He adds a preface to Sidonius’s book on the embassies, 73. He writes the miracles of Saint Martin after being warned in a vision, 993. Letter to his own people of Tours, 993. To Saint Sulpicius, 1269. To Saint Germanus, 1281. Fragments of commentaries on the Psalms, 1257. Book on the miracles of Saint Andrew, 1261. On the Passion of Saint Julian, etc., 1265. He translated into Latin the Passion of the Seven Sleepers of Ephesus, 829. Life of Saints Maurilius and Albinus, bishops, 1281. Antiphon concerning Saints Medard and Gildard, 1283. Life of Saint Aredius, 1283. Chronicles, 585. Works attributed to him, 1261. Epitome of the History by Fredegar, 541. Praised by Fredegar, 587. His reckoning differs from Fredegar’s, 595 n. In which month he begins the year, 731 n.

Gregory, patrician, 652. Griciense estate, 1309. Grifo stirs up disturbances, 685 n., 687. He is killed, 688. Grimo, abbot of Corbie, 681. Grimoald, 656. Duke, 657. Mayor of the palace of Austrasia, 658. He makes his son king and perishes miserably, 657 n. Grimoald, son of Pippin, becomes mayor of the palace, 670, 1353. He is killed, 671. His son Theudoald; his wife was the daughter of Ratbod, ibid. Grimoald, brother of Theodelinda, 610. Grindio fastened to a wheel, 229.

Grippo, ambassador to the emperor Maurice, 483, 484. Frank by birth, 484. Sword-bearer, 1346. He escapes death at Carthage, 484, 485, 488. Guaifarius. See Waifarius. Gualbert, abbot of the Greater Monastery, 1279, 1280. Guarinus, brother of Saint Leodegarius, 666 n. Gascony. See Vasconia.

Governor of the palace of Charibert II, 632. Gucilio, count of the palace, 229. Gudila, wife of Duke Wintrio, 390 n. Guernica, an island, 401 n. Guerpinus, count of Meaux, 391. Guiestremondus, 1291 n.

Gundeberga, wife of Charoald, 628. She is vindicated from injustice, 629, 630. Gundeberga marries Chrotar, 643. She is dismissed, 644. A parent of the Franks, ibid. Gundebert, son of Gundoald, 611. Gundegisil, bishop of Bordeaux, 476, 479, 504, 508. Metropolitan, 469. Said to have been a count of Saintonge, 395. Said to be Gundegisil Dodo, ibid.

Gundeland, mayor of the palace, 626, 1352. Gunderic, king of the Vandals, 44. Gundeuch, king of the Burgundians, 80, 556. Gundoald, brother of Queen Theodelinda, 610. His sons, 611. He is killed, ibid. Gundoald, duke, 575, 576.

Gundobad, king of the Burgundians, 855. Son of Gundeuch, 80. He consents to the marriage of Chlotild, 557, 558. Betrayed by his brother, he is driven out, 85, 561, 557, 559. He is besieged at Avignon, 86. Freed, he besieges his brother at Vienne, 87. He kills him, 88. He crushes the Franks, 562. He makes laws, 88. Secretly wishing to renounce Arianism, he is rebuked by Saint Avitus, 88. He asks Saint Avitus to write against the heresies, 89. Debate in his presence, 1322. He wavers, 88, 1323, 1325. He hardens himself, 1324. He perishes through fear of the people, 89. Unfortunate on account of heresy, 104. He dies, 107. Saint Sigismund succeeds him, 563.

Gundobad, son of Guntram, 164, 220 n., 569. He is killed, 570. Gundobald, commander of Sigibert’s army, is defeated, 591. He rescues Childebert II and establishes him as king, 201. Gundobald, count of Meaux, 391. Gundobaud, son of Saint Sigismund, 110 n. Gundoberga, daughter of King Agon, 611.

Gundovald Ballomer, 452, 840. His varied fortunes, 298, 299, 582. He was said to be Chlothar’s son, 297. Hated by his brothers, he joined Narses, 362. After taking a wife, he had two sons, 362, 451, 455. He departed with his sons for Constantinople, 362. He acts there, 363. Invited into Gaul by Guntram Boso, 358, 362, 363, 365. He seizes Rigunth’s treasures, 360. Sought by Childebert’s nobles, 358, 363. And recognized, 360.

He comes to Marseilles, 297, 298, 299. He is received by the bishop, 363. He is abandoned by Guntram, 363. Mummolus joins him, 298, 338. He is raised as king, 338, 341. Portents of his destruction, 339. Called Ballomer, 341. He visits the cities, 350. He said that he possessed sovereignty over Gaul, 377. He attempts to invade Guntram’s kingdom, 596. He is received by force at Toulouse, 332. He boasts that he is Chlothar’s son, 351, 362, 363, 582. And that he is king, 359, 363. His ambassadors, 355, 357. Friend of Bishop Bertram, 355. He takes the relics of Saint Sergius, 356. He appoints bishops, 357, 377. He deals with Brunichild, 359. He withdraws to Comminges, 359, 361. He deceives its citizens, 360. He is besieged, 361. He is subjected to insults, 362, 363. He is abandoned by his own men, 364, and betrayed, 365. He is killed, 366, 582, 597.

His possessions are plundered, 299, and his treasures, [Col. 1242] 361. Waddo possesses these treasures, 515. Guntram distributes them to the poor, 367, 378. Those who had joined him, 352, 359, 364, 384. The supporting bishops are punished at the Council of Mâcon, 392.

Gundulf, a household officer, becomes duke, 286, 300. Gregory’s uncle, 287. He takes possession of Marseilles, 288. Gundulf, messenger of Saint Germanus, 1345. Gundulf, citizen of Tours, 1088. Guntabund, king of the Vandals, 45 n., 50 n.

Gunthar, son of Chlodomer, 110, 564. He is killed, 565. Gunthar, son of Chlothar I, 142, 143, 567, 1089. The elder, 127. Gunthar, formerly an abbot and later bishop of Tours, 144, 535, 900. He dies, 148. Gunthegisel, 557. See Godegisel. Guntheuca, wife first of Chlodomer and then of his brother Chlothar, 110, 564. Gunthsuentha, queen of Spain, 179. Guntio, son of Magnacharius, is killed, 220 n., 570.

Guntram, king, 263, 286, 298, 413, 441, 442, from 162 to 538, 572, 574, 578, 585, from 595 to 601, 943. Son of Chlothar I, 142, 156, 157, 567, 568. His kingdom, 293. Seat at Orléans, 162, 569. He is solemnly received there, 375. He resides there, 457. He rules in Burgundy, 569. His wives and sons, 164, 569, 570. His sons, etc., 577. He is deprived of his sons, 221. He swears peace with his brothers, 575. Leaving Chilperic, he joins Sigibert’s party, 192. Likewise, 193, 194. Pact with Sigibert, 440. Victorious, he makes peace with Chilperic, 305. He loses several cities, 289. He invades Charibert’s kingdom, 339. Chilperic and Childebert conspire to bring about his destruction, 273. Chilperic takes cities from him, 296. His vision concerning Chilperic’s death, 380. After Chilperic is killed, he comes to Paris, 335. He receives Childebert’s ambassadors, 335. He protects Fredegund, 336. Joined with Childebert, 318. He praises him, etc., 379, and adopts him, 221. He loves him deeply, 446, 577.

His uncle and father, 385. He hands his kingdom over to him, 358. He instructs him and returns Sigibert’s cities to him, 359. The city of Albi, 415. He returns part of Marseilles, etc., 583. He uncovers a conspiracy against him, 427. Conversation with him, 429, 430, 598. His example, 439, 440. He receives his embassy, 340, and sends one, 384. Likewise on account of the birth of a son to Childebert, 409. He is abandoned by him, 581. He breaks peace with him, 289. He suspects Brunichild, 451, and Childebert as well, 455, 456.

His expedition, 349. The people of Poitiers surrender to him, 350. He retains Marseilles, 304, and returns it, 308. He restrains the Britons, 436, 437, 493, 494. They satisfy him, 437. He fears for himself, 337, 344. He repairs the damage inflicted by Chilperic, 344. Coming to Paris, he turns back, 496. He plans to go to Paris, 521. He comes here, 381, 522. He complains that Chlothar’s baptism has been delayed, 381, 382. He doubts his birth, 446. He lifts him from the sacred font and returns to Chalon-sur-Saône, 522. He wishes to govern his kingdom, 391. He establishes him in the kingdom, 597.

Adoptive father of kings, 340. He creates Celsus patrician, 163, and Mummolus, 182. He places the latter in command of the war, 188. The latter protects his kingdom, 184. Mummolus flees from him, 581.

Guntram’s ambassador to Spain, 338. From there he receives an embassy, 408. He rejects the ambassadors of Spain, 415. Of King Reccared, 419, 435. He wishes to avenge Ingund’s death, 435, 445. He refuses to give Chlodosind to Reccared, 444. Expedition into Septimania, 454. Unsuccessful, 455. He sends into Spain to avenge Saint Hermenegild, 397, 399. Expedition into Spain, 597. Unsuccessful, 600. His army plunders everything, 399. It perishes completely, 399, 400. Guntram punishes the commanders, 400, 401. His army takes Arles, 170. He possesses the province of Arles, 413 n. He refuses to march against the Lombards, 452, and to bring assistance, 445. His commanders crush the Lombards, 574. He receives Aptacharius’s embassy, 487. He recovers cities from a Lombard, 625.

Expedition against Gundovald, 351, 359, 360, 361, 362, 596, 597. His army devastates Septimania, 425. He pursues Gundovald, 299. He punishes his ambassadors, 355, and others as well, 357, 358. He pursues his friends too, 377, 378. He spares Baddo, 432. He receives Duke Beppolenus, 412. Duke Lupus flees to him, 274. His duke Erpo, 219. Patrician Mummolus, 214. Referendary Licerius, 411. His army, 300. Its wing (cornu), 971. He fears that he will be killed, 337. He uncovers Fredegund’s plot, 415. A conspiracy against him, 582. A conspiracy against him by Aegidius, bishop of Rheims, 513. He wishes to avenge Chilperic’s death, 379. He arranges the burial of his grandsons, 382. He returns to Chalon-sur-Saône, 383. He fulfills an impious oath, 244, 245. At his wife’s request, he kills physicians, 580. He confines Theudechild, 167. He banishes Bishop Munderic, 207. He persecutes Theodorus, bishop of Marseilles, 383, 384. He orders a bishop to be bound, 288. Childebert reserves Guntram Boso for his judgment, 426. He rages against him and against Bishop Magneric, 429, 430. He kills the sons of Magnacharius, 220, and Chundo the chamberlain for a trivial reason, 435. Hostile to Aegidius, bishop of Rheims, 433, and to Childeric the Saxon, 391.

Guntram convenes a synod, 470: at Paris, 190; at Lyons, 232; at Chalon-sur-Saône, 238; at Mâcon, 392. He investigates the killers of kings, 345. Pious works, 336, 337, 805. Goodness, 295, 376, 446, 595. He receives ambassadors at a feast, etc., 446, 376. He visits churches, ibid. He founds the basilica of Saint Marcellus, 595. He enriches it, establishes monks there, and ensures that they are confirmed by bishops, 596. His vision; he adorns Saint Marcellus’s tomb, 447 n. With a marvelous ciborium, etc., 1396. He attends the saint’s feast, 420, where a plot is prepared against him, 421. He founds the church of Maurienne, 1342, 1413. He favors the monastery at Poitiers, 473. He receives Chrodield, a nun, 468, 469. He did not sell priestly offices, 315. He orders public prayers, 446. He heals a fever-stricken person, etc., 447. His goodness toward bishops, 313, and his reverence, 233. He receives Bishop Praetextatus, 343. He orders an investigation into his killing, 404. He wants this case examined in a synod, 445. His piety in preserving the right of asylum of churches, 352. He suffers insults from Bishop Sagittarius, 233. He gives Gundovald’s treasures to the poor, 367. He falls gravely ill, 393. He dies, 601, 1135. He is venerated as a saint, 601 n.

Guntram, duke, 298, 577. He invited Gundovald into Gaul, 299. He besieges Avignon, 300. Guntram, duke of Sigibert, 193. Guntram, duke, 215. He takes refuge in the church of Saint Martin, 214. He is deceived by a pythoness, 216. He is accused of Theudebert’s death, 217, 218, 229. He flees with Merovech, 219.

Guntram Boso, duke, 214, 340, 578, 1048. Saint Martin saves him from shipwreck, 1049. Ambassador at Constantinople, 341. He joins Childebert, 235. His daughters, ibid., 236. He plots against Merovech, 217, 229. Accused, he flees, 394. He had invited Gundovald, 358, 362, 363. [Col. 1243] He plunders his treasures, 363, 365. Hated by Brunichild, 425. Condemned to death, 429. He is killed, 430, 448, 598. His vices, 430.

Gurthonense monastery, 970. Guto, a Lombard, 625 n. Gyges, king of the Lydians, 17. Gyso, count, 660.

## H
## H

H is equivalent to chapter 50, note.

## APPENDIX

The Appendix to the Works of Saint Gregory, Containing Ancient Monuments Which He Praises or Which Illustrate His Works. 1149  
[Col. 1303]

# Manuscript and Printed Codices Used for the Collation of the Works of Saint Gregory of Tours, and the Notes by Which They Are Designated

[Col. 1303]

In preparing the *History*, we used two Julian codices, one formerly from Corbie (Corb.), the other from Saint Peter of Beauvais (Bell.); one from the Royal Library (Reg.); two from the Colbert Library, one from the monastery of Metz (Colb. a), the other from Saint Michael’s (Colb. m); one from the monastery of Bec (Bec.); one from Regiomontium (Regm.); one from the abbey of Vendôme (Vind.); one from the monastery of Monte Cassino (Casin.); two Vatican codices (Vat. Alex.); one belonging to Cardinal Ottoboni (Ott.); the Palatine codex in Freher (Pal.); fragments from the royal and Colbert manuscripts, from Saint-Germain-des-Prés (Germ.), the College of Clermont (Clar.), Saint Vincent of Le Mans (Vinc.), the monastery of Marmoutier (Majm.), and others; and the printed editions of Badius (Bad.), Morel (Mor.), and his various readings (Mor. s.), Matthias Flacius Illyricus (Illyr.), *Christian History of the Ancient Fathers* (Bar.), Marquard Freher (Freh.), Bignius’s *Library of the Fathers* (Big), the Cologne edition (Col.), Bochellus (Boch), his various readings (Boch. s.), and Chesnius (Chesn.).

We collated the *Epitome of Fredegar* against the Sirmondian manuscript (Clar.) and one belonging to the illustrious Boherius (Boh.); and against the printed editions of Freher and Chesnius.

The *Chronicle*, likewise, was collated against the same manuscripts, and against one Colbert manuscript and one Vatican manuscript from the Palatine Library (Vat.); against the printed editions listed above for Gregory’s *History*, and against two Canisian codices.

The eight books of the *Miracles* were collated against the following manuscripts: one from Laon (Laud.), one from Beauvais, one Colbert manuscript (Colb. a); those of Pithou (Pith.) and Sanbovius (SB.); the royal manuscripts; the Colbert manuscript brought from Tulle (Colb. Tut.); another Colbert manuscript (Colb. c); another; two manuscripts from the College of Clermont (Clar. a, Clar. b); one formerly belonging to Queen Christina of Sweden and now to Cardinal Ottoboni (Rom.); one from the abbey of Vendôme; one from Saint Martin of Tours (Mart.); two from Marmoutier (Majm. a, Majm. b); five from Saint-Germain-des-Prés; one from Jumièges (Gem.); one from Saint-Victor in Paris (Vict.); one from the Vatican Library (Vat.); one from Saint-Corneille of Compiègne (Comp.); one from Saint Vincent of Le Mans; one from Fleury; one from Saint Gatianus of Tours (Gat.); one from Bec; and several others, which are noted in their proper places.

Among the printed editions, in addition to those already listed, we used those of Chlictoveus (Chlict.), Maternus Cholinus (Chol.), Balesdens (Bal.), Bollandus (Bol.), Surius (Sur.), Gononus (Gon.), and others.

We collated the *History of the Seven Sleepers* against one manuscript from Saint Victor and one from the College of Clermont, together with the printed editions.

The *Testament of Saint Aridius* is here published in full for the first time, from two manuscript copies belonging to Saint Martin of Tours and from the papers of Monsieur Mosnerius. For the appendix, among other codices, we used one Corbie manuscript written during the lifetime of our Gregory.

We collated the *Life of Saint Gregory* against three codices: one from Saint-Germain-des-Prés, one from Saint Paul of Cormery, and one from Saint Sergius of Angers.

## End of the Seventy-First Volume
